verdict_text: YES. The script drops exactly the 48 buffers by full-name match, casts exactly the 64 projection matrices to bfloat16 via float32, upcasts every remaining tensor to float32, keeps names unchanged, enforces all four required checks with assertions before writing, and writes a sharded safetensors checkpoint to `out/T3` with a 268,435,456-byte shard limit. Its correctness on the sharding layout and index file depends on the shared `save_sharded_safetensors` helper, which is not shown but is invoked with the specified limit.
